headline: Switzerland Survives Colombia's Wasteful Onslaught
story: Colombia imposed possession and offensive intent from the start, monopolising 56% of the ball and launching 15 attempts in a relentless assault on Switzerland's discipline. Yet the Swiss held firm in a compact shape, forcing 49 turnovers and recovering possession with sharp urgency every 13.6 seconds. Neither side broke through a deadlocked 90 minutes—a familiar dance of one team's dominance meeting another's resolute defence.

Colombia's 0.97 xG to Switzerland's 0.58 told the story of creation without conversion. Though the Colombians fashioned more dangerous openings and forced 52 turnovers, they could muster only three on-target efforts from 15 attempts—a wasteful conversion that proved fatal. Switzerland's poise under sustained pressure, forged through calculated high-press resistance (7.2 phases to Colombia's 6.0), carried them to clinical penalties where they won 4-3.

keyMoment.text: Full-time stalemate sends match to penalties, where Switzerland's composure prevails 4-3.

home.verdict: Defensive solidity and shootout nerve saw off Colombia's toothless dominance.
points: Forced 49 turnovers and recovered possession every 13.6 seconds—negated Colombia's possession advantage.
Two shots on target from seven attempts: efficiency, not volume, won the shootout.
Risk survived: 0.58 xG was vulnerable to one Colombian finish; penalties rewarded composure.

away.verdict: Wasteful finishing in open play sent penalties to fortune's lottery.
points: Fifteen shots yielded three on-target; one more finish settles it inside 90 minutes.
0.97 xG translated to zero goals—conversion rate was the fatal deficit.
Recovery time 16.6s cost possession rhythm; sharper transitions could have exploited space.

statLine: Colombia fired 15 times for 0.97 xG; Switzerland absorbed it all and won 4-3 on penalties—nullification's ultimate vindication.
